1. Present appeal is filed against order dated

11.06.2018 passed by Learned District Consumer

Commission (Nomenclature of District Consumer Forum converted

to District Consumer Commission vide new
Consumer Protection Act
2019) in consumer complaint No.166/2015 titled Harish

Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. Versus Harish Kumar
F.A. No.193/2018
Kumar Versus The Motor Claim Manager Bajaj Allianz

General Insurance Company Ltd.
Brief facts of consumer complaint:
2. Shri Harish Kumar complainant filed consumer

complaint under
Consumer Protection Act
pleaded therein

that complainant is owner of vehicle No.HP-78-0491. It is

pleaded that vehicle was insured with opposite party w.e.f.

23.01.2014 to 22.01.2015. It is pleaded that vehicle met with

accident on 23.10.2014 and rapat No.11 dated 26.10.2014

was also registered in police station Nangal. It is further

pleaded that at the time of accident vehicle in question was

driven by Shri Surinder Kumar driver. It is pleaded that

information of accident was given to opposite party. It is

pleaded that complainant submitted Insurance claim before

Insurance company but Insurance company repudiated

Insurance claim and committed deficiency in service.
Complainant sought relief of payment of Rs.350000/-(Three

lac fifty thousand). In addition complainant sought relief of

payment of Rs.100000/-(One lac) as compensation for mental

agony and torture. In addition complainant sought costs of

litigation to the tune of Rs.30000/-(Thirty thousand). Prayer

for acceptance of consumer complaint sought.
3. Per contra version filed on behalf of opposite party

pleaded therein that complainant has sold vehicle in question
2
Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. Versus Harish Kumar
F.A. No.193/2018
to Shri Surinder Kumar on dated 22.07.2014 in consideration

amount of Rs.168000/-(One lac sixty eight thousand) and

complainant has no insurable interest in vehicle in question

at the time of accident. It is pleaded that accident took place

on 22.10.2014 and information was given by complainant on

24.10.2014. It is pleaded that opposite party did not commit

any deficiency in service. Prayer for dismissal of consumer

complaint sought.
4. Learned District Consumer Commission ordered

opposite party to pay a sum of Rs.105523/-(One lac five

thousand five hundred twenty three) to complainant within

thirty days from receipt of copy of order alongwith interest @

9% per annum from the date of filing of complaint. Feeling

aggrieved against order passed by Learned District Consumer

Commission opposite party filed present appeal before State

Commission.
5. We have heard learned Advocates appearing on

behalf of parties and we have also perused entire record

carefully.
6. Following points arise for determination in present

appeal.
1. Whether appeal filed by appellant is liable to be
 accepted as mentioned in memorandum of
 grounds of appeal?
2. Final order.
3
Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. Versus Harish Kumar
F.A. No.193/2018
Findings upon point No.1 with reasons:
reasons:
7. Complainant filed affidavit Annexure-C1 in

evidence. There is recital in affidavit that deponent is owner

of vehicle in question. There is recital in affidavit that vehicle

in question was insured with Insurance company w.e.f.

23.01.2014 to 22.01.2015. There is recital in affidavit that

vehicle met with accident on dated 23.10.2014 and vehicle

was badly damaged. There is recital in affidavit that matter

was reported in police station Nangal vide Rapat No.11 dated

26.10.2014. There is recital in affidavit that deponent has

engaged one Shri Surinder Kumar as driver in vehicle in

question at the time of accident. There is recital in affidavit

that Insurance claim was submitted before Insurance

company but Insurance company repudiated the claim and

committed deficiency in service. State Commission has

carefully perused all annexures filed by complainant.
8. Opposite party filed affidavit of Shri Ankur Jindal

Annexure-R1 in evidence. There is recital in affidavit that

vehicle in question met with accident on 23.10.2014 at

Balmeek Chowk Naya Nangal. There is recital in affidavit that

vehicle in question at the time of accident was registered in

the name of Shri Harish Kumar complainant. There is recital

in affidavit that Sh. Harish Kumar has sold the vehicle in

question to Sh. Surinder Kumar on 22.07.2014 in
4
Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. Versus Harish Kumar
F.A. No.193/2018
consideration amount of Rs.168000/-(One lac sixty eight

thousand). There is recital in affidavit that at the time of

accident Sh. Surinder Kumar was driving vehicle in question.
9. Opposite party also filed affidavit of Sh. Navjeet

Singh Assistant Manager in evidence. There is recital in

affidavit that consumer complaint is not maintainable

because at the time of accident complainant sold vehicle in

question to Shri Surinder Kumar on dated 22.07.2014 in

consideration amount of Rs.168000/-(One lac sixty eight

thousand) and complainant has no insurable interest in

vehicle in question at the time of accident.
10. Opposite party also filed affidavit of Shri Satish

Kumar Surveyor cum Loss Assessor in evidence. There is

recital in affidavit that deponent physically inspected vehicle

in question and assessed loss to the tune of Rs.105523/-(One

lac five thousand five hundred twenty three). State

Commission has carefully perused all annexures filed by

opposite party.
11. Submission of learned Advocate appearing on

behalf of Insurance company that complainant sold vehicle to

Shri Surinder Kumar at the time of accident and complainant

has no insurable interest in vehicle in question at the time of

accident and on this ground appeal filed by Insurance
5
Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. Versus Harish Kumar
F.A. No.193/2018
company be allowed is decided accordingly. We have carefully

perused R.C of vehicle in question annexure-C6. As per R.C.

ownership of vehicle is in the name of Sh. Harish Kumar

complainant as of today. As per
section 2(30)
of Motor

Vehicles Act owner means a person in whose name a motor

vehicle stands registered and where such person is a minor

the guardian of such minor and in relation to a motor vehicle

which is the subject of a hire-purchase agreement or an

agreement of lease or an agreement of hypothecation the

person in possession of the vehicle under that agreement. As

per R.C. vehicle in question was leased with KCC Bank

Lathiani Himachal Pradesh. State Commission is of the

opinion that as per law lessor is not legally competent to

transfer leased vehicle to third person without the consent of

lessee. State Commission is of the opinion that complainant

was not legally competent to transfer vehicle to third person

without the consent of lessee i.e. KCC Bank Lathiani. There

is no evidence on record in order to prove that complainant

has sought permission of lessee prior to selling of vehicle in

question. It is held that sale of vehicle to third person by

lessor without consent of lessee is void ipso facto.
12. State Commission is of the opinion that there are

two types of ownership (1) De jure ownership (2) De facto

ownership. It is held that De jure ownership means a person
6
Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. Versus Harish Kumar
F.A. No.193/2018
in whose name vehicle in question is registered as per R.C. as

mentioned under
section 2(30)
of Motor Vehicles Act 1988 at

the time of accident. It is held that De facto ownership means

a person who is in actual possession of vehicle in question at

the time of accident. It is well settled law that when there is

conflict between De jure ownership and De facto ownership

then De jure ownership always prevail over De facto

ownership in view of
section 2(30)
of Motor Vehicles Act 1988.
See AIR 2018 SC 983 titled Naveen Kumar Versus Vijay

Kumar (Full Bench). See AIR 2018 Allahabad 128 titled Amar

Nath Chaubey Versus State of U.P. It is well settled law that
section 2(30)
of Motor Vehicles Act 1988 refer to De jure

ownership and does not refer to De facto ownership.
13. It was held by Hon'ble High Court of H.P in case

reported in latest HLJ 2019 (HP) 232 titled The Oriental

Insurance Company Ltd. Versus Durga Dass & Anr. that

Insurance company could not be exonerated from liability

when vehicle was transferred to new owner but Insurance

policy was still in the name of previous owner. It was further

held in case reported in 2018(4) CLT 612 SCDRC Haryana

titled Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. Versus Vishav

Pal and others that if R.C and Insurance policy are in the

name of complainant at the time of accident then Insurance

company could not be exonerated from liability simply on the
7
Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. Versus Harish Kumar
F.A. No.193/2018
ground that vehicle was sold to third person by complainant

and simply on the ground that complainant has no insurable

interest.
14. It is proved on record that Insurance company

also appointed Surveyor cum Loss Assessor namely Shri

Satish Kumar and Sh. Satish Kumar has submitted report

under section 64UM of statutory
Insurance Act
1938. Sh.

Satish Kumar has assessed damage to the tune of

Rs.105523/-(One lac five thousand five hundred twenty

three). State Commission is of the opinion that damage

assessment report submitted by Surveyor cum Loss Assessor

is trustworthy, reliable and inspire confidence of State

Commission. Insurance company did not send any

interrogatories to Surveyor cum Loss Assessor namely Shri

Satish Kumar appointed under section 64UM of statutory
Insurance Act
1938. State Commission is of the opinion that

Insurance company is under legal obligation to pay O.D claim

as assessed by Surveyor cum Loss Assessor appointed under

section 64UM of statutory
Insurance Act
1938.
15. Submission of learned Advocate appearing on

behalf of Insurance company that there is three days delay in

filing FIR and on this ground appeal filed by Insurance

company be allowed is decided accordingly. As per report

submitted by Surveyor cum Loss Assessor under
section
8
Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. Versus Harish Kumar
F.A. No.193/2018
64UM of statutory
Insurance Act
1938 present Insurance

claim is a genuine claim. State Commission is of the opinion

that Insurance company is under legal obligation to pay

genuine claim of complainant. See 2019(1) CPR 471 NC titled

ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Ltd. Versus

Honest Bio-vet Pvt. Ltd. See AIR 2017 SC 4836 (DB) titled

Om Prakash Versus Reliance General Insurance & Anr. See

2019(1) CPR 725 NC titled Assistant Commissioner

Commercial Tax Versus New India Assurance Company Ltd.
16. Submission of learned Advocate appearing on

behalf of Insurance company that learned District Consumer

Commission has discarded investigation report and on this

ground appeal filed by Insurance company be allowed is

decided accordingly. State Commission is of the opinion that

report submitted by Surveyor cum Loss Assessor under

section 64UM of Statutory Insurance Act 1938 is a

substantial piece of evidence for adjudication of dispute inter

se complainant and Insurance company and Surveyor cum

Loss Assessor has assessed O.D claim of vehicle to the tune of

Rs.105523/-(One lac five thousand five hundred twenty

three).
17. Submission of learned Advocate appearing on

behalf of Insurance company that complainant was under
legal obligation to give information to insurer relating to
9
Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. Versus Harish Kumar
F.A. No.193/2018
transfer of vehicle in question as per
section 157
of Motor

Vehicles Act alongwith provision of GR-17 of Indian Motor

Tariff and on this ground appeal filed by Insurance company

be allowed is decided accordingly. State Commission is of the

opinion that transfer of leased vehicle by complainant without

consent of lessee i.e. KCC Bank Lathiani is ipso facto void

transfer under law because vehicle in question was stood

leased with KCC Bank Lathiani as per entry recorded in R.C

of vehicle in question. It is held that complainant was not

legally competent to transfer leased vehicle in question

without consent of lessee i.e. KCC Bank Lathiani.
18. Submission of learned Advocate appearing on

behalf of Insurance company that present matter is governed

under
Sales of Goods Act
and ownership of vehicle in question

was changed from date of intention of sale and on this ground

appeal filed by Insurance company be allowed is decided

accordingly. State Commission is of the opinion that
Motor

Vehicles Act
1988 is a
Special Act
which governs vehicles

disputes only. It is well settled law that when there is conflict

between Special Law and General Law relating to vehicle then

Special Law always prevail over general law.
19. Submission of learned Advocate appearing on

behalf of complainant that order of learned District Consumer

Commission is in accordance with law and is in accordance
10
Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. Versus Harish Kumar
F.A. No.193/2018
with proved facts and does not warrant interference by State

Commission is decided accordingly. State Commission is of

the opinion that order of learned District Consumer

Commission is strictly in accordance with laws and is in

accordance with proved facts and does not warrant

interference by State Commission in view of fact that vehicle

in question was already leased with KCC Bank Lathiani as

per R.C. placed on record and in view of fact that lessee did

not give any consent to complainant to alienate vehicle to

third person. Point No.1 is decided accordingly.

Point No.2: Final Order
20. In view of findings upon point No.1 above appeal is

dismissed. Order of learned District Forum (Nomenclature of

District Consumer Forum converted to District Consumer Commission

vide new
Consumer Protection Act
2019) is affirmed. It is ordered

that Insurance company shall pay O.D claim of vehicle in

question to complainant as ordered by learned District Forum

(Nomenclature converted to District Consumer Commission

as per
Consumer Protection Act
2019) after production of

NOC from KCC Bank Lathiani. It is further ordered that if

complainant will not produce NOC from lessee i.e. KCC Bank

Lathiani in that eventuality Insurance company shall

transmit O.D claim of vehicle in question to KCC Bank

Lathiani for liquidation of loan amount. Parties are left to
11
Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. Versus Harish Kumar
F.A. No.193/2018
bear their own litigation costs before State Commission.

Insurance company will comply order within one month after

receipt of certified copy of order.
21. Report of Surveyor cum Loss Assessor namely

Satish Kumar Annexure-R19 dated 09.12.2014 and R.C. of

vehicle in question Annexure-C6 shall form part and parcel of

order. File of learned District Consumer Commission

alongwith certified copy of order be sent back forthwith and

file of State Commission be consigned to record room after

due completion forthwith. Certified copy of order be

transmitted to parties forthwith free of costs strictly as per

rules. Appeal is disposed of. Pending application(s) if any

also disposed of.
Justice P.S. Rana (R)
 President
